issue.title: Question: How does pylint resolve imports?

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
## Question

This may or may not be the right place for this, but I am deeply confused about how imports work across pylint, mypy and python itself and am having trouble coming up with a regime that seems to work consistently across all three. I would greatly appreciate some clarifying guidance.

In this case, I have a structure like this:
```
namespace/
  pkg/
    __init__.py
    subpkg/
      __init__.py
      resource.py
      example.py
```
namespace is a PEP 420 namespace. pkg is a collection of other packages. subpkg is where the actual goodies are.

I had been writing my import statements *entirely explicitly*, e.g. in example.py:
```
from namespace.pkg.subpkg import resource
```

And then, generally, installing my package in development mode. This worked out okay for a while, except mypy gets confused because it believes that `./example.py` and `namespace.pkg.subpkg.example` are two different modules sometimes when there are circular imports. It appears as if sometimes this code gets loaded twice, because the development mode installation treats the "real" file and the reference to the "real" file as two different things.

I have started switching -- but have not yet fully switched to -- using implicit relative imports. This seems to make mypy a lot happier overall. e.g. example.py again:
```
import resource
```

The problem I am now seeing, however, is that pylint sometimes cannot find these imports anymore.
PYTHONPATH for me is completely unset, it is whatever the default is under my virtual environment.

```
> which pylint
/home/user/.local/share/virtualenvs/development-3q2gnOaG/bin/pylint
> cd ~/src/namespace/pkg/subpkg/
> pylint example.py
example.py:1:0: E0401: Unable to import 'resource' (import-error)
```

It works at runtime just fine, and it works from a python shell in the venv, too.
(From the subpkg dir):
```
>>> import resource
# Works OK
>>> from namespace.pkg.subpkg import resource
# Also OK
```

if I set PYTHONPATH to `.` it starts to work again. Shouldn't pylint be looking in my current dir by default for implicitly relative imports? Why is it not?

Advice or troubleshooting tips deeply appreciated, I seem to keep getting my import regime wrong on a daily basis :(

EDIT: This appears to be a problem with pylint 2.5.0, 2.5.1, and 2.5.2. This is subtly just a little different from the bug I filed concerning *explicit* relative imports, which appears to only be a problem with pylint 2.5.1, 2.5.2, and 2.5.3.

Explicit relative import bug: https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/3624
Related (?) import bug: https://github.com/PyCQA/pylint/issues/3651 (Filed against 2.5.2)

issue.title: false-positive: E0401 import-error for relative imports inside __init__.py (but only sometimes)

labels.name: Duplicate 🐫
labels.description: Duplicate of an already existing issue

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
### Bug description

### Description
Relative imports inside a `__init__.py`file cause random E0401.

E.g.:
Say one has a module A.B.C.D inside a folder `src` such that
- All the required `__init__.py` files exist for modules A, B, C and D
-  `src/A/B/C/D/some_moduleX.py` exists and defines `SomeClassX` where `X=1,2,3`
- Content of `src/A/B/C/D/__init__.py` contains
```
from .some_module1 import SomeClass1
from .some_module2 import SomeClass2
from .some_module3 import SomeClass3
```
pylint will issue E0401 (pseudo-)randomly for **some** of the imports, even if all of them are similar. For which one the warnings are issued depends on the version/machine used - e.g. GitHub actions uses pylint v.2.11.1 and gives me different locations and a different amount of E0401.
If there are only a few relative imports across the entire project, pylint might not issue E0401 at all.

Python code using this module works flawlessly. E.g. via `from A.B.C.D import SomeClass2` 

### Workaround
Adding a `.pylintrc`
```
[MASTER]
init-hook='import sys; sys.path.append(".")'
```
fixes the issue.

### Sad Note
I tried to come up with a minimalistic example with nested modules all containing relative imports in the `__init__.py` files importing dummy classes from the same level but for some reason this bug could not be provoked that way. I tried for quite a while but this is the best I can do.

### Related
- #3984
- #4226

### Configuration

_No response_

### Command used

```shell
pylint src
```


### Pylint output

```shell
************* Module src.A.B.C.D
src/A/B/C/D/__init__.py:2:0: E0401: Unable to import 'src.A.B.C.D.some_module2' (import-error)

# NOTE: The exact output is inconsistent across versions/machines.
```


### Expected behavior

no warnings

### Pylint version

```shell
pylint 2.10.2
astroid 2.7.3
Python 3.9.7 (default, Oct 10 2021, 15:13:22)
[GCC 11.1.0]
```
